issues.description: setuptools<82 added to core runtime install_requires instead of build-only constraint
issues.detail: The cap belongs to the build environment (mmcv/mmengine still call pkg_resources, which setuptools 82 removed). Putting setuptools<82 into core/setup.py extras pins the constraint on every downstream consumer of autogluon.core forever, not just CI. The invariant being maintained here is 'mmcv build needs old setuptools'; that invariant lives at build time, not at the runtime dependency of a published package. A literate comment explaining why this cap exists, and ideally moving it to a CI/build constraints file rather than install_requires, would be more honest about what is being asserted.

issues.description: Version-pinning rationale is under-commented at the point of decision
issues.detail: Three separate files now carry a setuptools<82 pin, but only two carry the FIXME pointer to mmcv issue 3325. core/setup.py has no comment at all explaining why a runtime dep is capped. A reader six months from now, asked to bump dependencies, will see a bare 'setuptools<82' and have to do archaeology. Literate-programming-grade fix: one line of comment at each pin pointing to the upstream issue and the condition under which the cap can be removed.

issues.description: mmcv installed with --no-build-isolation silently changes the build contract
issues.detail: Switching from `mim install mmcv==2.1.0` to `pip install mmcv==2.1.0 --no-build-isolation` means mmcv is now built against whatever setuptools/torch/numpy happen to be in the ambient environment rather than the isolated build env pip would normally construct from pyproject.toml. The invariant 'mmcv builds successfully' now depends on prior installation order in this script (setuptools<82 must already be present, torch must already be importable, etc.). That ordering constraint should be stated explicitly in a comment above the install line, or the script will break the next time someone reorders these three pip calls.

issues.description: mmdet bumped 3.2.0 -> 3.3.0 without explanation in the diff
issues.detail: The PR title and the surrounding comments are about mmengine/setuptools. The mmdet version bump is a separate change folded into the same commit with no stated reason. Either it is forced by the new mmengine pin (in which case say so) or it is unrelated drift (in which case it should be its own change). A reviewer auditing this PR cannot tell which from the diff alone.

issues.description: Two FIXME comments point at the same upstream issue but only one states the revert condition
issues.detail: env_setup.sh says 'remove cap once fixed'; setup_mmcv.sh says 'revert mmcv installation to use mim once fixed'. core/setup.py says nothing. A future maintainer resolving issue 3325 has to grep three files and reconstruct the full set of reversions. A single named marker (e.g. a comment tag like MMCV_3325_WORKAROUND) at every site would make the cleanup mechanical rather than archaeological.

review.summary: Decision: UNDER-AUDITED. The change correctly identifies the root cause (setuptools 82 removed pkg_resources, which mmcv/mmengine still import) and applies a reasonable pin-and-pivot fix. The algorithmic content is sound: cap setuptools at build time, install mmengine from the PyPI wheel rather than a git SHA, drop mim in favor of direct pip with --no-build-isolation. My concerns are about literate-programming hygiene and where the invariant is asserted: a build-time constraint has leaked into core/setup.py's runtime install_requires, the --no-build-isolation switch introduces an ordering invariant that isn't stated, the mmdet 3.2.0 -> 3.3.0 bump is unexplained, and the three pin sites share a workaround but only two share the explanation. The fix ships; the explanation that future maintainers need to unwind it does not yet.
